narrative.headline: Top 50 tilts decisively bullish — 22 BULLISH names led by mega-cap tech and defensives, with 17 BEARISH concentrated in financials, energy, and staples.
bullish_setups: AAPL: $38M call premium + $4.2B dark pool — score 9.75
MSFT: $31M flow + $5.0B dark pool, highest DP print in scan
NVDA: $35M near-money call premium + $3.1B dark pool
AMZN: $23M flow + $2.8B dark pool — clean accumulation
PLTR: $17M call premium + $1.4B dark pool, score 9.63
ORCL: $30M flow stands out vs $543M DP — aggressive option positioning
INTC: $18M flow + $4.1B dark pool — contrarian rebuild
LLY: $20M call premium + $834M DP — healthcare leader bid
JNJ/PG: perfect 10.0 composites — defensive rotation confirmed
bearish_setups: GOOGL/GOOG: both flow ~3.1 — distribution diverges from broader mega-cap tech bid
BAC/WFC/MS: financials cluster bearish (flow 2.1–3.8) despite C being top-5 bullish
XOM: flow 3.53 — energy supermajor under put pressure
WMT: flow 1.73, weakest in scan — staples leader being sold
PEP: flow 4.05, score 2.43 — staples split with PG
RTX/GEV: defense/industrial names seeing put-side flow
narrative.rotation_signal: Institutions are accumulating mega-cap tech (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, ORCL, PLTR), semis (KLAC, INTC), and defensives (JNJ, PG, LLY) while distributing big banks (BAC, WFC, MS), Google complex, energy (XOM), and WMT. The C vs BAC/WFC/MS split and PG vs PEP/WMT split suggest name-specific selection rather than blanket sector calls.
narrative.diverging_from_industry_layer: GOOGL/GOOG bearish read conflicts with otherwise dominant mega-cap tech bid. Financials are bifurcated — C strongly bullish while BAC/WFC/MS bearish, worth flagging against any broad-bank industry signal. INTC bullish despite typical semis-laggard framing.
